summary: Pickle Lake Airport (YPL) is a medium-sized regional airport serving the remote community of Pickle Lake in northwestern Ontario, Canada. The airport plays a vital role in connecting this isolated mining and First Nations community to the rest of the province, supporting both passenger travel and the region's significant gold mining industry. It also serves as an important hub for medical evacuations and cargo operations in an area with limited road access.
faqs:
Q: How do I get to Pickle Lake from the airport?
A: The town of Pickle Lake is only a short drive from the airport. Car rentals are limited and should be arranged in advance, though local taxi services and hotel shuttles are available with prior notice.

Q: What airlines serve Pickle Lake Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by regional carriers offering scheduled flights to Thunder Bay and other northern Ontario destinations. Wasaya Airways and Bearskin Airlines have historically operated routes in and out of YPL.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: Yes, Pickle Lake Airport operates throughout the year, though winter weather can occasionally cause delays. The airport is equipped for all-season operations given its importance to the remote community.

Q: Are there facilities like food or lounges at the airport?
A: The terminal is small with limited amenities. Travelers should plan accordingly, as there is no on-site restaurant and services are basic.
transport_tips: Given the remote location, flying is often the most practical way to reach Pickle Lake, as road travel from Thunder Bay takes approximately 7-8 hours on a partially unpaved highway. Arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended, as rental cars and taxis are not always available on short notice. The airport is located just a few kilometers from the town center, making the trip into Pickle Lake quick once you arrive.
local_tip: If you're heading out to one of the nearby gold mines or fly-in fishing lodges, confirm your charter or shuttle arrangements before arrival—cellular service is extremely limited in the area, and Wi-Fi at the terminal can be unreliable for last-minute bookings.
